externalRef: Tier Standard: Topology (Tier I to Tier IV objectives)
externalTitle: Basic capacity; Redundant capacity components; Concurrent maintainability; Fault tolerance
notes: A Tier objective describes site-infrastructure behaviour during maintenance and failure. It does not define capability Service Outcomes, performance or integrity tolerances.
Tier selection reflects business need but the standard does not define criticality criteria.

externalRef: Tier Standard: Operational Sustainability (planning, coordination and management)
notes: Capacity planning is an operational-sustainability concern; demand modelling for AI loads is AIDCF-specific.
Operating the site within design load overlaps the load envelope; environmental and state-specific limits are AIDCF parameters.
TCCF outcomes are E5 evidence that the constructed facility demonstrated the design topology at the time of certification. They do not establish current configuration or post-certification changes.

externalRef: Tier Standard: Topology (Tier III and Tier IV)
externalTitle: Independent distribution paths; Fault tolerance and compartmentalisation
notes: Path independence and compartmentalisation address shared-source and shared-route common mode for power and cooling; common controllers and human dependencies require AIDCF analysis.

externalRef: Tier Standard: Topology (engine-generator as primary power)
notes: The Tier concept that on-site generation is the reliable source bounds utility dependency; telecom, OEM and cloud dependencies are out of scope.
Site-location risk factors overlap site hazard assessment and adjacent risk.
Compartmentalisation overlaps fire and water zone intent for site infrastructure; security zoning and tenant segregation are out of scope.

aidcfFamilyName: Fire, life safety and emergency interfaces

notes: Utility is not relied upon for Tier objectives; utility capacity and grid quality remain AIDCF evidence items.

externalTitle: Engine-generator capacity and on-site fuel; Operations
notes: Engine-generator as the primary power source with on-site fuel overlaps strongly; start reliability and fuel replenishment need operational evidence.
UPS redundancy within the Tier topology overlaps; battery condition and runtime derating are operational.
Distribution path redundancy and concurrent maintainability overlap; selective coordination and earthing are engineering-study items.
Maintenance programmes overlap preventive maintenance; switching procedures and black-start are AIDCF items.
Cooling redundancy and continuous cooling overlap resilient capacity; seasonal derating needs site evidence.
Air distribution within the white space is largely outside Tier topology evaluation.
Application of Tier concepts to CDUs and secondary liquid loops should be confirmed with the Tier Standard owner.
Heat-rejection redundancy and on-site water provisions overlap; water continuity from utility is AIDCF evidence.

externalRef: Tier Standard: Operational Sustainability; Topology (continuous cooling)
notes: Maintenance and continuous cooling overlap thermal recovery intent; sensor trust and control stability are AIDCF-specific.

externalRef: Tier Standard: Operational Sustainability (staffing and organisation)
notes: Staffing levels, qualifications and organisation overlap strongly.

externalRef: Tier Standard: Operational Sustainability (planning, coordination and management)
notes: Procedures and coordination overlap SOPs and method statements; permit to work is governed by safety regulation.
Preventive maintenance programme and practices overlap strongly; calibration and deferred-maintenance governance need explicit evaluation.
Failure response and lessons learned are part of operations practice; alarm rationalisation is AIDCF-specific.

externalRef: Tier Standard: Operational Sustainability (planning, coordination and management)
notes: Change coordination overlaps change assessment; configuration baselines are AIDCF-specific.
Load and capacity management overlap capacity review.
Tier objectives express a resilience intent for site infrastructure only; minimum service outcome of the AI capability is AIDCF-specific.
Fault tolerance and compartmentalisation overlap containment for power and cooling; compute, storage and network fault domains are out of scope.

externalTitle: Demonstrations of concurrent maintainability or fault tolerance
notes: TCCF demonstrations are E4/E5 evidence for component tests at the time of certification; integrated AI-capability scenario tests are AIDCF-specific.
Spares may be considered within maintenance practice; lead times and obsolescence are AIDCF-specific.
Operational Sustainability certification is time-bounded and renewed; AIDCF evidence expiry and decision suspension operate independently of the certification cycle.
